Redesigning the Connector Studio UI off user feedback calling it unintuitive, with a phased rollout over late Oct and Nov 2026.

cases.title: Multi-tenant data platform for US + EMEA banks

metric.label: infra cost removed; onboarding + GTM cut by 90 days

cases.summary: Lead platform PM for a multi-tenant, config-driven data platform (DPaaS) serving enterprise banks in the US and EMEA. Banks onboard by subscription with zero code changes.
evidence: Owned the full design of the Data Platform SaaS: architecture, boundaries, integrations and vendors, data flows and contracts, subscription model, onboarding, configuration format and UI.
Defined and enforced a multi-tenant, config-driven, ephemeral DAG architecture; mandated subscription-based onboarding and said no to client-specific builds.
Banks onboard through subscription-based, config-driven setup: 0 code changes, 0 engineering-led builds, standardized deployment workflows.
Eliminated the MongoDB dependency, saving ~$50K a year in recurring infrastructure cost.

Made data freshness a per-tenant config tied to its AWS cost; drove cost vs freshness tradeoffs across S3, real-time Kafka, API and batch ingestion, dbt/Airflow orchestration and provisioned vs serverless compute.
Cut client onboarding + GTM by 90 days (4 months to 1 month) with reusable ETL/ELT pipelines, standardized playbooks and integration guides.

Established data contracts and a governed semantic layer across 1,200+ attributes and 20+ schemas: lineage, replication strategy, freshness guarantees, PII/PCI DSS/GDPR controls and sanctions/AML data flows (OFAC, FinCEN).
Codified platform guarantees and non-guarantees: SLAs, quality, ingress and egress strategy, sequencing; canonical ingestion, modelling and transformation patterns.

Owned the connector portfolio: 12+ connectors live across DigiFi, Equifax, TransUnion, MoEngage, FeatureSpace FRM, Qualco, Xero, Decta, GoCardless, AWS Connect, core processor and banking partner warehouses.
A client subscription provisions a DAG per tenant-vendor combination, replacing per-client integrations and cutting GTM by months.

Defined a 1-year roadmap across 120+ business requirements from enterprise banking clients, achieving a 95% delivery rate against strategic OKRs.
Closed 70+ data quality gaps in 2 months; reached a 0-incident steady state; escalations down 70% and CSAT up from 2.5 to 4.0.
Replaced a manual reporting bottleneck with self-serve analytics for finance teams: reporting time down from 1 week to 5 minutes.
Authored architecture documentation across 600+ attributes, driving CardWorks' $3M+ credit card portfolio data migration.
Co-owned an analytics product launch with HDFC: DAU/MAU, transaction and dispute tracking dashboards.
Established data governance as a platform layer: RBAC, test cases and lifecycle policies.

projects.name: Track
projects.tagline: A calm, ad-free live tracker for Indian trains and flights.
evidence: Built because train trackers fired 266 requests and megabytes of ads to answer 'where is my train?'.
The hero is the traveller's stop, not the train's raw position; flight screens reshape by phase (gate, map, baggage belt).
One Cloudflare Worker normalises five sources (crowd-sourced running feed, NTES, IRCTC seats, AeroDataBox, live ADS-B) into one shape, so the frontend never knows who answered.
Stretches a free-tier flight-data quota across all users with shared caches and a daily budget; stale data is labelled, never passed off as exact.
Searches 8,677 stations on-device; no ads, sign-ups, cookies or analytics; installable, no build step.

projects.name: Shelfie
projects.tagline: A reading tracker you drive with your thumbs.
evidence: Books are arcade passes you flick through, drag up to turn pages and drop onto shelves; every move is a spring that keeps the finger's speed.
Offline-first, with optional accounts using passkeys and end-to-end encrypted sync on a Cloudflare Worker and D1.
Two-minute Goodreads import, synthesised sound and haptics (no audio files), 20 badges, and motion controls tuned on real iPhone recordings.

projects.name: Decoding Credit Cards
projects.tagline: 22 interactive chapters on how credit cards actually work.
evidence: 22 interactive chapters: tap a card to watch a transaction settle, drag a slider to watch compound interest grow.
Design system, content and code built end-to-end in plain HTML, CSS and JS with zero dependencies; free, no login, no ads, no card recommendations.

projects.name: Zero to a Hundred
projects.tagline: An open, vendor-neutral curriculum for learning AI in 21 phases.
evidence: 21 phases from Python and Git through classic ML, how LLMs work, RAG, agents and MCP, to evals, security and inference economics.
154 concepts and 105 curated resources; about 90% of resources are free.
Each phase states what you can do when it's done and asks you to build something before moving on.

evidence: An AI-native interaction layer on top of Jira as the system of record: same data, workflows and integrations.
Three surfaces: an action-first home, conversational ticket creation with maker-checker preserved, and natural-language dashboards that write JQL.
Every AI output is auditable: signals used, plain-English reasoning, a confidence number and the cost of being wrong.
Includes a 13-slide product teardown and 3 role personas.

projects.name: GRID
projects.tagline: An editorial reference for Formula 1's 2026 reset, with live timing.

Live page pulls positions, fastest laps, weather and race-control flags from OpenF1; any one feed can fail without taking the others down.

projects.name: The Cookbook
projects.tagline: 216 high-protein dishes that start from context, not chapters.

A fridge matcher ranks dishes by the ingredients you have; cook mode keeps the screen awake with timers.
Treated as a data product: 216 cards, an ingredient database, 421 aliases and a relationship graph; a validator blocks deploys if any card's macros disagree with the database.
